title: P75 (Papyrus Hanna 1): Luke 4:34-5:10 (fols. 9r-9v)
source: Papyrus Hanna 1 (Mater Verbi), Vatican Library: photographs from DigiVatLib; Greek from the INTF NTVMR transcription of P75; English from the King James Version
description: Luke 4:34-5:10 in P75 (Papyrus Hanna 1), the papyrus codex of Luke and John copied around 175-225: fols. 9r-9v, each page with its photograph, the Greek transcription and the King James Version.
introduction:
P75 is a papyrus codex of Luke and John copied in Egypt around 175-225, the oldest known copy of Luke and one of the oldest of John. It was bought by Martin Bodmer in the 1950s and published as Papyrus Bodmer XIV-XV; in 2006 it was given to the Vatican Library, where it is kept as Papyrus Hanna 1 (Mater Verbi). Its text is very close to that of Codex Vaticanus, written some 150 years later. Where Luke ends and John begins (folio 44r) both titles stand on the same page.

About 51 leaves survive, many damaged at the top and edges, especially in Luke 3-7. Lost: Luke 1:1-3:17, most of 3:23-4:33, 5:11-36, 6:5-10, 7:33-34 and 7:44-45 (and parts of 7:36-49), 17:16-19, 18:19-22:3; John 11:46-47, 12:1-2, 13:11-14:7 and everything after 15:10 except small fragments. Each section below is one page: the photograph, the NTVMR diplomatic transcription line by line, and the King James Version of every verse on the page. Where P75 lacks a verse or words that the KJV has (for example John 5:4 or the account of the adulteress, John 7:53-8:11), the section says so. Six damaged pages (folios 7v, 11r, 39v, 58r, 58v and 64v) are left out because their text could not be matched to the photographs with certainty.

This entry covers fols. 9r-9v (Luke 4:34-5:10), shown on the Vatican Library's photographs (frames 1A.3r to 1A.3v).
translator_notes: Greek: the NTVMR diplomatic transcription, line by line as on the papyrus. Square brackets enclose letters that are lost or illegible and were supplied by the transcribers; a dot under a letter marks it as uncertain; [...] marks a gap. Nomina sacra and numerals keep the scribe's overline. Spelling is the scribe's (no accents or breathings). Words broken at a line end stay broken as on the papyrus. Corrections are not shown: the text is the first hand.

English: the King James Version (1611), whole verses, for every verse that has text on the page. A verse that begins on one page and ends on the next is given in full on both. The KJV translates a later form of the Greek text, so its wording does not always match the papyrus; material differences (such as verses the papyrus does not have) are noted in the section.

translation.text: <sup>4:34</sup>Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art; the Holy One of God. <sup>35</sup>And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him. And when the devil had thrown him in the midst, he came out of him, and hurt him not. <sup>36</sup>And they were all amazed, and spake among themselves, saying, What a word is this! for with authority and power he commandeth the unclean spirits, and they come out. <sup>37</sup>And the fame of him went out into every place of the country round about. <sup>38</sup>¶ And he arose out of the synagogue, and entered into Simon’s house. And Simon’s wife’s mother was taken with a great fever; and they besought him for her. <sup>39</sup>And he stood over her, and rebuked the fever; and it left her: and immediately she arose and ministered unto them. <sup>40</sup>¶ Now when the sun was setting, all they that had any sick with divers diseases brought them unto him; and he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them. <sup>41</sup>And devils also came out of many, crying out, and saying, Thou art Christ the Son of God. And he rebuking them suffered them not to speak: for they knew that he was Christ. <sup>42</sup>And when it was day, he departed and went into a desert place: and the people sought him, and came unto him, and stayed him, that he should not depart from them.

NTVMR page 40 (folio 9r). 4:34 begins on the previous page; 4:42 continues on the next page. Checked on the image: the frame is pencilled 'Luc IV, 34-42'; on the upper right fragment δαιμο[νια] (4:41) can be read, matching the transcription of this page.

translation.text: <sup>4:43</sup>And he said unto them, I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent. <sup>44</sup>And he preached in the synagogues of Galilee. <sup>5:1</sup>And it came to pass, that, as the people pressed upon him to hear the word of God, he stood by the lake of Gennesaret, <sup>2</sup>And saw two ships standing by the lake: but the fishermen were gone out of them, and were washing their nets. <sup>3</sup>And he entered into one of the ships, which was Simon’s, and prayed him that he would thrust out a little from the land. And he sat down, and taught the people out of the ship. <sup>4</sup>Now when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught. <sup>5</sup>And Simon answering said unto him, Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net. <sup>6</sup>And when they had this done, they inclosed a great multitude of fishes: and their net brake. <sup>7</sup>And they beckoned unto their partners, which were in the other ship, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the ships, so that they began to sink. <sup>8</sup>When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord. <sup>9</sup>For he was astonished, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken: <sup>10</sup>And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
